# ISSUE-370: task-local Chromium profile

Enable preview and Chromium commands through approved-base policy in the existing native Linux Bubblewrap executor. Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive; retain the human plan gate. This revision addresses all five maintainer findings without changing the acceptance criteria.

## Scope and budget

Use one boolean (`execution.browser_profile`), one fixed 2 GiB memory cap, the existing internal-tools startup flags, one systemd user scope per command, and one shell fixture. No new policy descriptor, transient service, configurable limits, network setup, npm fixture dependency, browser tool, or general runtime framework. Codex's shell, OCI and other platforms remain outside scope.

Estimated total: planning 1h, policy/propagation 2h, scope/executor and adversarial tests 5h, validation/preflight/bundle 2h, docs/fixture 1h, independent review and focused validation 2h: 13h within the 16h total claim budget, leaving 3h contingency. Reassess against actual remaining claim time before implementation; reopen rather than widen if a scope cannot safely preserve process lifecycle or the estimate no longer fits. Renewals remain coordinator-owned and bounded by approved policy.

## What we know

- `internal/contract/execution.go:17` defines ExecutionConfig; ResolveExecution validates native/OCI and isolated/trusted-local choices. Add the boolean here, not to the WorkUnit schema or repository defaults.
- `internal/sandbox/executor.go:25` defines ToolExecutor; command at :37 configures verified process cancellation. executorFlags at :74 uses `--unshare-all`, `--die-with-parent`, cap-drop ALL, clearenv, read-only dependencies and an 8 GiB address-space limit. Run at :151 enforces two minutes and retains cache use on unverified stop. Preserve those semantics.
- CheckToolExecutor at `internal/sandbox/executor.go:181` includes positive-controlled host-loopback, synthetic secret/symlink, environment and read-only canaries. Reuse their bodies under the profile.
- `internal/sandbox/delegated.go:182` builds the executor; internalToolArgs at :254 already serializes `--share-host-dependency-caches`. `internal/cli/internal_tools.go:12` reconstructs it. OMP uses the in-process executor; Claude/OpenCode use serialized startup arguments.
- `internal/sandbox/validation.go:17` selects Codex validation by tester harness; availability, canary, cache reuse and execution must all prefer Bubblewrap when browser policy is enabled.
- Approved configuration loads through `internal/harness/scaffold.go:575`, `internal/workflow/engine.go:391`, `internal/workflow/execute_setup.go:90` and bundle compilation at `internal/workspace/worktree.go:848`.
- `internal/sandbox/toolchain.go:266` discovers Playwright cache; `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:82` marks node-browsers no-prefetch. Existing mounts are read-only. No package installation is needed to run cached chrome-headless-shell directly.
- Preclaim entry is `internal/workflow/engine.go:315`; doctor checks are in `internal/cli/doctor.go:154`; bundle entry is `internal/workspace/worktree.go:789`. Process stop implementation is `internal/process/tree_unix.go:18`.
- Snapshot searches confirm proposed browser helper/test/fixture and changelog paths below are absent. This environment has no .git, so approved-commit existence cannot be independently verified here.

## What we're assuming

- Supported hosts provide systemd user scopes with cgroup v2 memory accounting and Chromium shared libraries. A disposable scope using the same launcher verifies enforcement and an actual cached-browser launch; unsupported hosts fail production preflight with actionable errors.
- Private loopback already works under `--unshare-all`, as the maintainer confirmed. The positive HTTP fixture verifies it; add no lo activation, capability, or namespace sharing.
- Existing dependency provisioning can expose the cached headless shell. Check the resolved node-browsers cache rather than assuming any browser cache contains Chromium.

## Open questions

- Can the host verify actual scope membership, memory.max and memory.swap.max before executing the payload, and verify teardown afterwards? Step 2 answers this with deterministic failure tests and gated live execution. Missing live infrastructure is recorded for review, not an implementation prerequisite.
- Actual remaining claim time and live harness availability are coordinator facts unavailable in this snapshot. Record elapsed budget and live results in review evidence; do not claim authenticated runs were performed here.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. **Policy and transport.** Modify `internal/contract/execution.go` ExecutionConfig/ResolveExecution and `execution_test.go`: optional boolean browser_profile, false by default, enabled only for isolated native execution. Reject malformed YAML and incompatible execution choices. Extend approved-base parsing coverage in `internal/harness/scaffold_test.go`. Carry the resolved value through existing configured runner/adapter options (`internal/agent/configured.go`, `adapters.go`, `isolated.go`, `internal/sandbox/worker.go` WorkerOptions). Set ToolExecutor.BrowserProfile in `delegated.go`; append hidden `--browser-profile` in internalToolArgs and parse it in `internal/cli/internal_tools.go`. This is coordinator startup data like cache flags, never a swarm_shell JSON parameter, environment override or candidate config read. Extend corresponding tests for Claude/OpenCode and direct OMP propagation. Do not add a descriptor or grant protocol.
2. **Fixed memory boundary.** Add `internal/sandbox/browser_linux.go`, `browser_other.go`, and `browser_test.go` for a small Linux-only launcher and unsupported-platform errors. Use structured argv `systemd-run --user --scope` with unique per-command unit, MemoryMax=2147483648 and MemorySwapMax=0. Keep the synchronous scope launcher in the tracked process tree; never use a detached service. A trusted pre-exec helper in the same swarm executable (hidden internal command in modified `internal/cli/internal_tools.go`) checks its actual /proc/self/cgroup membership and corresponding cgroup-v2 effective limits before execing Bubblewrap. Do not trust property-setting success, candidate paths or payload assertions. Reject missing/unlimited/wrong limits, wrong membership and unreadable state; recheck every invocation after preflight. Construct a minimal launcher environment with only required user-manager connection data, no coordinator credentials; clear that data before Bubblewrap. Keep manager sockets and cgroup filesystem outside payload mounts. Retain `--die-with-parent`, process.Configure and StopVerified. After normal exit, startup error, timeout or cancellation, stop any remaining scope members and verify the group empty; join cleanup errors and retain cache use when cleanup is unverified. Use existing safe process/path practices; no production verification bypass.
3. **Executor and fixture.** Modify `internal/sandbox/executor.go` command/executorFlags/Run/CheckToolExecutor and `executor_test.go`. Only the verified profile path drops `--as=8589934592`; all other limits, mounts, namespaces, output bounds and default flag ordering remain unchanged. Factor existing canary execution to accept profile options without weakening checks. Resolve cached chrome-headless-shell from validated node-browsers dependencies; test a real launch with --no-sandbox. Add `internal/sandbox/testdata/browser-preview.sh`: one shell invocation creates a small page, starts `python3 -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1`, waits for readiness, runs cached chrome-headless-shell with --no-sandbox and fresh task-local user-data directories, saves --dump-dom and --screenshot output plus logs, asserts rendered text and PNG, and traps server cleanup. No Node/Playwright package import, npm install or download; Playwright only provisions the host cache. Two browser invocations inside one shell command may produce DOM and screenshot. Private loopback needs no setup. Validate browser state is local and caches remain read-only.
4. **Availability, validation and guidance.** Modify `internal/sandbox/validation.go` nativeValidationUsesCodex and its callers so enabled policy selects Bubblewrap for availability, runtime checks, cache reuse and execution, including Codex testers; preserve disabled routing and validator discard/cache behavior. Extend `internal/validation/validator_test.go` and existing submission tests to prove failed browser required checks block submission through the existing ErrRequiredCheckFailed path. Modify preflight in `internal/agent/configured.go`, `internal/workflow/engine.go`, and `internal/cli/doctor.go` to report requested/available with missing bwrap, cached shell or verified cap reasons before lease writes; use existing approved-base config flow and recheck at execution. Modify `internal/workspace/worktree.go` and `bundle_guidance_test.go` with approved-policy-conditioned developer/tester one-command instructions and output-file guidance. Codex instructions direct browser checks through validation. No new check type or CI substitution.
5. **Docs and release note.** Modify `docs/project.md`, `docs/harness/claude.md`, `opencode.md`, `omp.md`, `codex.md` and `SECURITY.md`: real YAML field, Linux systemd/cgroup prerequisites, host Playwright Chromium installation, existing read-only cache configuration, direct cached headless-shell/Python command and two-minute lifetime. Explain --no-sandbox with Bubblewrap as the boundary. Add `changes/unreleased/370.md` in neighboring fragment format. Verify CLI/config examples against source and shell syntax. Record live fixture runs for all three delegated harnesses in PR review evidence, including unavailable prerequisites when necessary.

## HANDOFF

This is planning evidence; verify against approved source and gates before implementation. Production source was not changed during planning. Human plan approval remains required by WORKUNIT.md before implementation.

Entry points and references: ExecutionConfig (`internal/contract/execution.go:17`), ToolExecutor/command/executorFlags/Run/CheckToolExecutor (`internal/sandbox/executor.go:25`, :37, :74, :151, :181), internalToolArgs (`internal/sandbox/delegated.go:254`), internal-tools (`internal/cli/internal_tools.go:12`), native validation (`internal/sandbox/validation.go:17`), PreflightForClaim (`internal/workflow/engine.go:315`), bundle (`internal/workspace/worktree.go:789`). Exact focused commands and ownership are in TEST_PLAN.md.

Extend TestGoConcurrencyExecutor, TestToolExecutorBoundary, TestMCPToolCancellation, TestDelegatedValidationWithoutCodex (`internal/sandbox/executor_test.go:363`, :90, :46, :19), TestBundleGuidanceApprovedBase (`internal/workspace/bundle_guidance_test.go:228`), TestDoctorRejectsUnavailableSelectedAgent (`internal/cli/doctor_test.go:46`), existing config/cache/preflight/validator/submission tests. Add new cases under TestBrowserProfile for focused selection. Independently review the sensitive boundary.

Checked: inspected startup serialization and native validation routing directly; searched cache classification and approved config loading; confirmed new paths absent in supplied snapshot. Before creating those paths, coordinator/developer must check `git cat-file -e <approved-base>:<path>` in the Git-backed checkout; if present, inspect and modify instead. No approved-base absence claim is made from this snapshot alone.

Reopen if scope parent/lifecycle cannot preserve verified stop, cap verification requires a new runtime framework, propagation requires new authority, any extra host mount/network/capability is needed, or work cannot fit remaining budget. Do not weaken adversarial tests or silently drop acceptance coverage.

### What this change breaks

Repository searches for internalToolArgs, node-browsers, nativeValidationUsesCodex and the executor tests identified these dependencies:

- TestGoConcurrencyExecutor asserts default address-space limits: preserve unchanged; add enabled assertions separately.
- `internal/sandbox/build_cache_test.go:636`, `dependency_cache_test.go:876`, `private_modules_test.go:201` serialize startup flags: preserve disabled output; add enabled roundtrip coverage with CLI parsing.
- `internal/sandbox/delegated.go:153` and `internal/agent/telemetry_session_test.go` use default canaries: retain default behavior; exercise same probes under profile.
- `internal/sandbox/validation.go` and cache/executor tests depend on Codex selection: preserve disabled cases; add enabled routing and failure coverage.
- `internal/sandbox/toolchain.go:266` and dependency-cache tests depend on node-browsers classification: preserve read-only/no-prefetch, add headless-shell availability checks.
- Bundle approved-base/role-filtering tests: add enabled guidance and preserve candidate-tampering protections.
- Listed harness/project/security docs describe default isolation: update opt-in behavior only. Repository defaults, scaffold policy templates, WorkUnit schema and CI policy remain unchanged.

# ISSUE-370 test plan

Developer records revision, commands, results and runtime skip reasons. Tester independently reviews source and acceptance, reusing applicable passing results. Repeat checks only for relevant changes, observed failures or an unresolved coverage concern. New focused tests use TestBrowserProfile prefixes. Preserve existing adversarial assertions.

## Acceptance mapping

| Criterion | Cases and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 1: one command, DOM/screenshot, trusted opt-in | Policy/flags tests cover omitted/false, approved true, malformed YAML, OCI/trusted-local rejection, exact disabled flags and all retained limits. Approved-base tests cover candidate enabling/disabling without effect; WorkUnit/env/tool JSON cannot enable. Transport tests roundtrip browser flag through internalToolArgs/CLI for Claude/OpenCode and direct OMP executor, without a new descriptor. Gated preview test runs browser-preview.sh as one swarm_shell command and one native required check, asserts rendered DOM and PNG, unchanged read-only cache and no download. Uses cached chrome-headless-shell + python3 http.server only, no npm package. |
| 2: boundary, cap and lifecycle | Run unchanged CheckToolExecutor probes under enabled profile. Shell and Chromium tests deny host-loopback, DNS and outside addresses, with positive host controls to distinguish isolation from ambient offline status; local HTTP succeeds. Check synthetic host/coordinator env and file/symlink/proc sentinels remain hidden, no manager socket/cgroup mount or desktop/profile exposure. Unit-test scope argv, verified actual membership/limits before payload exec, missing/unlimited/wrong cap, manager failure, per-command recheck and no marker execution on failure. Live memory test touches more than 2 GiB only inside verified scope, observes cgroup OOM and supervisor survival. Timeout/cancellation tests run browser and server plus detached descendants, verify process disappearance, closed ports and no delayed markers; normal exit/startup failure also leave an empty scope. Cleanup failure retains caches. Confirm synchronous --user --scope, --die-with-parent and StopVerified remain in use. No loopback setup. |
| 3: native validation and submission | Table-test enabled/disabled routing for Codex and delegated tester harnesses across availability, canary, execution and cache reuse. Real gated passing/failing browser assertions run through Bubblewrap validation. Assert ErrRequiredCheckFailed/report failure and existing submission refusal. Multi-check test proves other required commands still execute; unavailable profile errors rather than skipping commands. Candidate config cannot change validation policy. Preserve validator cache separation and discarded candidate modifications. |
| 4: doctor, dry-run, preclaim, bundle | Inject missing bwrap/cache/memory-controller or unverifiable cap; assert requested/available reporting, actionable reason and zero claim writes for work/preflight, including dry-run. Test prerequisites changing after probe fail execution. Doctor identifies inspected config context; work uses approved base. Bundle tests cover approved-base enabled developer/tester guidance, one-command/file-output examples, disabled and other-role filtering, and Codex validation-only wording. |
| 5: docs, tests and harness evidence | Check YAML through actual parser; commands/flags against registered CLI or browser/Python help, changed bash snippets with bash -n, relative links/anchors. Check all four harness guides, project docs, SECURITY boundary and changelog. Coordinator records make check. PR checklist records live fixture under claude/opencode/omp with versions, result and artifact references, or exact unavailable prerequisite requiring maintainer follow-up. External runs remain review evidence and never replace required checks. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

Run after relevant implementation is complete, with gofmt on changed Go files:

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/contract ./internal/harness -run 'Test(BrowserProfile|.*Execution.*)' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent ./internal/cli ./internal/workflow ./internal/workspace ./internal/validation -run 'TestBrowserProfile' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/sandbox -run 'Test(GoConcurrencyExecutor|MCPToolCancellation|DelegatedValidationWithoutCodex|ToolExecutorBoundary)' -count=1
SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1 go test -timeout=10m ./internal/sandbox ./internal/validation -run 'TestBrowserProfile' -count=1
go test -race -timeout=10m ./internal/sandbox ./internal/workflow -run 'TestBrowserProfile' -count=1
go vet ./internal/contract ./internal/harness ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent ./internal/cli ./internal/workflow ./internal/workspace ./internal/validation
bash -n internal/sandbox/testdata/browser-preview.sh
```

Run exact names of changed existing tests not selected above and record them. Parse extracted changed documentation shell examples with bash -n and configuration examples through real config tests. Do not execute provisioning/download commands in the sandbox.

Live tests are gated by SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1. Check infrastructure first and skip with a specific reason for missing runtime, cached headless shell/libraries or scope controller. Once prerequisites pass, a failed assertion is a failure, never a skip. Use deterministic test-only injected manager/cgroup results for unsupported and cleanup paths; no production bypass. Never launch the memory hog outside the verified capped scope. No network access or loopback activation is needed for the preview fixture.

## Tester-owned independent review

Read source against every criterion, concentrating on approved-base authority versus internal startup data, pre-exec actual scope membership/limits, synchronous parent lifecycle, verified stop/group emptiness, credential clearing, unchanged disabled flags/canaries and Codex validation selection. Inspect actual validation-to-submission failure handling, not just mocked executor outcomes. Review DOM/PNG, OOM and process-cleanup evidence. Reuse relevant developer passes; run additional focused checks only for a documented gap, failure or changed source. Record unavailable live coverage without treating it as success or blocking implementable unit coverage.

## Coordinator-owned reference policy

After roles finish, coordinator runs the complete trusted-base required policy once on the final candidate and records claim-bound validation. It is not a per-role checklist. Record the WorkUnit's make check requirement once and reuse overlapping results where supported. Agent observations remain advisory; they do not authorize publication or satisfy claim-bound validation. Human plan approval and renewal/submission remain existing coordinator operations.

## PR review checklist

- [ ] Approved-base existence checks for browser_linux.go, browser_other.go, browser_test.go, testdata/browser-preview.sh and changes/unreleased/370.md recorded; existing paths handled as modifications.
- [ ] Focused checks, independent sensitive-boundary review and make check results recorded, including runtime skips.
- [ ] Claude live fixture: harness/version, result, DOM/PNG/log references or unavailable prerequisite.
- [ ] OpenCode live fixture: harness/version, result, DOM/PNG/log references or unavailable prerequisite.
- [ ] OMP live fixture: harness/version, result, DOM/PNG/log references or unavailable prerequisite.
- [ ] No descriptor/service/npm dependency/loopback activation introduced; approved budget and gates respected.

VERDICT: APPROVED

Revised plan addresses all review notes.
